description: Rubs, marinades and sauces so the same batch protein does not taste identical all week. Rub amounts are per 5 lb (2.3 kg) of bone-in chicken or per 2 lb ground meat unless stated.
salting: Use about 3/4 tsp Diamond Crystal kosher salt (or 1/2 tsp Morton) per lb of raw meat. The old 3 tbsp per 5 lb was over 2x too salty.

marinades.name: Soy-honey-ginger
marinades.ingredients: 1/2 cup soy sauce, 1/4 cup honey, 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tbsp grated ginger, 4 cloves garlic; for 3-4 lb; 2-8 h

marinades.name: Yogurt marinade
marinades.ingredients: 1 cup plain Greek yogurt, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tbsp curry or garam masala, 1 tsp salt, 3 cloves garlic; 4-12 h
marinades.note: Acid and dairy tenderize lean breast. Do not marinate over 24 h.

marinades.name: Lime-cilantro
marinades.ingredients: 1/3 cup lime juice, 1/4 cup oil, 1/2 cup cilantro, 4 cloves garlic, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp salt; 2-6 h

marinades.name: Balsamic-garlic
marinades.ingredients: 1/3 cup balsamic, 1/4 cup olive oil, 4 cloves garlic, 1 tbsp Dijon, 1 tsp salt; 2-8 h

sauces.name: Soy + honey (current bowl sauce)
sauces.ingredients: 2.5 tsp soy sauce + 2 tsp honey per bowl

sauces.name: Peanut sauce
sauces.ingredients: 2 tbsp peanut butter, 1 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp lime juice, 1 tsp sriracha, water to thin

sauces.name: Yogurt-garlic sauce
sauces.ingredients: 1/2 cup Greek yogurt, 1 grated garlic clove, lemon juice, salt, dill or cucumber

sauces.name: Buffalo
sauces.ingredients: 1/2 cup hot sauce + 2 tbsp melted butter or oil

sauces.name: Green salsa
sauces.ingredients: Store-bought tomatillo salsa; about 10 kcal per 2 tbsp

spiceBudgetNote: Cheapest way to stock a rotating spice rack is the bulk or international aisle: cumin, chili powder, smoked paprika, garlic powder, oregano and curry powder cover 6 of 7 rubs above.
